statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of public unauthenticated templates. Authenticated profile, messaging, matching, payment, and account-deletion flows were not accessible without credentials; these exclusions are explicit in paths/report.md.

page.framework: Server-rendered legacy MPA with small JavaScript bundles
page.notes: Russian mobile dating site. Public surfaces are server-rendered; login/registration are protected by Cloudflare Turnstile.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, screenshot comparison, and DOM/CSS inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the light capture; body and form surfaces remain fixed pale cream/white and the DOM CSS contains no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rule.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated reduced motion and queried document animations/CSS
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() returned no active animations; the audited pages use no non-essential motion or auto-advance.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated prefers-contrast: more screenshot plus axe color-contrast audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more capture does not adapt the palette, and axe measured five failures including 1.98:1 for the h1 and 2.49:1 for the cookie button.

checkOutcomes.method: Navigated representative MPA routes and inspected page CSS
checkOutcomes.evidence: Navigation among home, registration, recovery, reviews, and help performs abrupt full-document swaps; DOM/CSS inspection found no ::view-transition rules or view-transition-name usage.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/CSS inspection and screenshots across long reviews and static pages
checkOutcomes.evidence: No parallax, scrollytelling, entry reveal, carousel, or other scroll-linked motion exists on the audited public templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no scroll-linked effect to implement declaratively.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/CSS inspection across representative paths
checkOutcomes.evidence: The public unauthenticated templates expose ordinary links/forms only, with no swipe, pull-to-refresh, draggable, snap-carousel, or gesture-driven component.
checkOutcomes.reason: No custom gesture interaction is present on the audited surfaces.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile screenshot and DOM inspection of long listing
checkOutcomes.evidence: The long reviews listing has no sticky context, progress, or scroll-state response; its only menu is at the top while pagination appears after the list.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM inspection across home, registration, recovery, reviews, and help
checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip, attached popover, dropdown, or edge-sensitive overlay is exposed on the audited unauthenticated templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no anchored overlay whose positioning can be judged.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual review and link/heading DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Headings, explicit action labels, numbered registration progress, back links, and review pagination identify the current context and next location without ambiguous icon-only navigation.

checkOutcomes.method: Initial mobile screenshot and DOM overlay inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: A fixed cookie banner occupies roughly the bottom 148px of the 800px mobile viewport on load and presents only a prominent Accept action, obscuring app-store/footer content.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered DOM inspection of the consent surface
checkOutcomes.evidence: The cookie control is a custom <span role="button" tabindex="0"> inside fixed divs, with no dialog/popover semantics and no light-dismiss or reject action.

checkOutcomes.method: Desktop/mobile screenshots and layout review
checkOutcomes.evidence: The unauthenticated pages are visually sparse and devote nearly all non-consent space to login, registration, help, or review content rather than decorative application chrome.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile layout metrics and screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: At 360x800 the layout primitive reported scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 and horizontalOverflowPx=0; mobile screenshots show controls reflowing without clipping.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS capability probe plus desktop/mobile screenshot comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS inspection found no container queries or logical sizing; at 1365px the login form remains a 244px strip while background panels stretch edge-to-edge, showing no component-level adaptation.

checkOutcomes.method: Focus/target-size probe and registration DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Every login control, recovery link, and registration field has tabindex=-1, removing the core flows from sequential keyboard navigation; many links are only 14–17px tall and the checkbox is 13x13px.

checkOutcomes.method: First-viewport screenshots and heading/action inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The first viewport identifies the service as mobile dating and exposes sign-in plus a clearly labelled free-registration action; the signup promo has one explicit next step.

checkOutcomes.method: Walked login/signup paths, inspected controls, and attempted empty registration submission
checkOutcomes.evidence: The login and two-step registration journeys cannot be completed with sequential keyboard input because all controls are tabindex=-1; Turnstile also gates both flows and the invalid registration attempt produced no actionable state.

checkOutcomes.method: Invalid-submit interaction plus 404 screenshot/DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: After accepting consent and attempting an empty registration submission, the page remained unchanged with no :invalid fields, role=alert, aria-invalid, or error text; the 404 tells users to go back but provides no actionable link.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile Lighthouse plus desktop trace and mobile layout observers
checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 4.3s and FCP 3.7s, outside the good range, although the local desktop trace was faster at 1.35s and CLS remained low.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse and first-load layout-shift observer
checkOutcomes.evidence: Observed CLS was 0.037 in Lighthouse and 0.059 in the mobile layout capture, both within the good range; screenshots showed no disruptive content jump.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse and DevTools trace summary
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse TBT was 0ms; the trace found one 84.57ms long task and 34.57ms total blocking time, a light main-thread result.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against actual head script attributes
checkOutcomes.evidence: Two 300KB+ parser-inserted legacy scripts in <head> have neither async nor defer; HAR recorded 31 requests, seven redirects, and 484KB transferred, with Turnstile alone delaying about 1.39s.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse code-coverage diagnostics and HAR weight breakdown
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 225KiB of unused JavaScript: 128KB from index.min.js, 54KB from Yandex Metrika, and 48KB from vendor-index.min.js.

checkOutcomes.method: axe-core plus rendered DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: axe reported critical label failures for both login fields, an unnamed tracking link, and missing landmarks; registration fields likewise use nearby text rather than associated <label> elements.

checkOutcomes.method: axe-core computed contrast audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: axe found five serious contrast failures, including the 1.98:1 heading, 1.79:1 online count, 3.94:1 sign-in button, 3.26:1 policy link, and 2.49:1 consent button.

checkOutcomes.method: axe structure audit and active focus/tabIndex probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: axe found no main landmark and content outside landmarks; more critically, login and registration inputs/buttons are all tabindex=-1 despite showing an outline only when focused programmatically.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed CSS and mobile screenshot inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The primary h1 is rendered at 13px and the consent text at 12px/14px; screenshots show dense low-contrast copy and edge-to-edge rows that reduce reading comfort.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM meta inspection, target-size probe, and mobile screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home, signup, registration, recovery, and help omit the viewport meta; the target probe found 13x13 and 14–17px-high controls, while core CAPTCHA canvas interaction has no equivalent exposed in page markup.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse console-error audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse observed no browser console errors or uncaught exceptions during load.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM, Lighthouse asset audits, and images primitive
checkOutcomes.evidence: The doctype and charset are valid, but 5 of 6 images omit width/height, four below-fold images are not lazy, and five use legacy PNG/GIF without responsive sources.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices diagnostics
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reports five BFCache blockers (notably Cache-Control: no-store and WebSocket use) plus DevTools cookie issues; deprecated APIs, paste prevention, and on-load permission prompts did pass.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM metadata inspection across representative templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home has a descriptive title/description, but signup, registration, recovery, and help have no meta description and reviews uses a blank description.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/link probes, robots.txt, and Lighthouse SEO corroboration
checkOutcomes.evidence: Links and robots.txt are crawlable, but four of five representative legacy templates omit meta viewport; several app-store links rely solely on images.

checkOutcomes.method: Fetched robots.txt, sitemap.xml, headers, and page canonicals
checkOutcomes.evidence: Responses and canonicals are valid, but the sitemap index lists only http:// URLs and every lastmod is 2021-09-12 despite currently changing profile/review content.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM metadata probe across landing and reviews
checkOutcomes.evidence: No JSON-LD or Open Graph tags were present on the organization landing page or public review listing, despite these representing a service/organization and user reviews.

checkOutcomes.method: Security headers and cookies primitives
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are all absent; sid and test cookies lack Secure and SameSite protection.

checkOutcomes.method: Initial screenshot, trackers, cookies, and HAR summary
checkOutcomes.evidence: While the only consent UI is still visible, Yandex Metrika and LiveInternet load; HAR recorded 25 of 31 requests and 468KB of 484KB from other origins, including repeated Yandex cookie-sync chains.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse permission audits and auth DOM/platform inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse confirms no geolocation/notification prompt on load, but both public authentication and registration expose password-only flows; no WebAuthn/passkey capability is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Main-document security header inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither CSP frame-ancestors nor X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Trusted Types enforcement, or origin-isolation headers were observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML versus rendered DOM discoverability capture
checkOutcomes.evidence: The raw response contains title, h1, description, form content, and core links; discoverability measured 80% content coverage and isJsShell=false, so primary public content survives without JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/layout/Lighthouse review across representative pages
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited public templates are server-rendered, use ordinary links/forms, fit at 360px without clipping, and produced no console errors; no fragile menu/overlay positioning was observed beyond separately reported consent semantics.

checkOutcomes.method: Fetched manifest and queried service-worker registrations
checkOutcomes.evidence: This app-like dating service exposes a manifest, but it contains only name "App" and one 192px icon, with no start_url/display/short_name; no service-worker registrations exist.

checkOutcomes.method: Navigated a missing route and inspected 404 state plus service-worker registrations
checkOutcomes.evidence: The real 404 returns status 404 and explains the problem, but offers only plain-text instructions to go back, no Home/Retry link; no offline fallback is registered.

checkOutcomes.method: axe, DOM, and CSS capability inspection across templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home, recovery, reviews, and registration use xml:lang or no language instead of a valid HTML lang attribute; axe flags html-has-lang, and the CSS capability probe found no logical properties.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered reviews DOM and time-element inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The reviews template renders Russian relative dates such as “вчера в 21:54” in <time> elements without datetime values, leaving no machine-readable instant and no evidence of locale-aware formatting.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/text inspection across representative templates
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited public/auth/help templates expose no scheduled event, recurring interval, absolute appointment time, or other user-editable time-zone-sensitive concept.
checkOutcomes.reason: No time-zone-sensitive task is present on the audited public surfaces.

checkOutcomes.method: Initial screenshot, consent DOM, cookies, trackers, and HAR evidence
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent banner offers only Accept while analytics and cookie syncing already run; there is no Reject or Settings control, making the apparent choice non-reversible and non-neutral.

checkOutcomes.method: Invalid registration interaction, screenshot, and state probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: After accepting terms and attempting an empty registration submission, no visible error, :invalid field, aria-invalid state, role=alert, or focused recovery target appeared; the CAPTCHA remained in “Verifying...” state.

checkOutcomes.method: Form attribute probes across login and registration
checkOutcomes.evidence: Login and registration text/password/date fields have empty autocomplete values and tabindex=-1; fields rely on nearby text rather than explicit labels, preventing autofill and keyboard assistance.

checkOutcomes.method: Auth/registration walkthrough and DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited account-creation/sign-in flows are password-only, keyboard-inaccessible, gated by a canvas CAPTCHA, and combine terms, cookies, and personal-data consent into one required checkbox.

checkOutcomes.method: Images primitive and HAR resource summary
checkOutcomes.evidence: Five images use legacy PNG/GIF, five omit intrinsic dimensions, four below-fold images are not lazy, and no image uses srcset; transferred image weight is modest at 36KB but delivery is not optimized.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse unused-code and HAR network analysis
checkOutcomes.evidence: A simple server-rendered login page transfers 428KB of script and Lighthouse estimates 225KiB unused; analytics triggers multiple cookie-sync redirects before consent.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR and tracker-origin analysis
checkOutcomes.evidence: 25 of 31 requests and 468KB of 484KB transferred came from other origins; Yandex, Cloudflare, and LiveInternet account for substantial script/network activity on a minimal login view.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected forms, metadata, and platform globals for agent tool registration
checkOutcomes.evidence: No developer intent or public agent-facing workflow was declared; this emerging capability is not required for the audited conventional dating/auth site.
checkOutcomes.reason: Agent-facing capabilities are contextual and the site declares no agentic intent.

checkOutcomes.method: Inspected platform globals and representative page tasks
checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation, generation, translation, or other inference task is part of the audited public login/registration/help journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no user task on these public surfaces that calls for on-device inference.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline and post-interaction heap-summary comparison plus runtime memory metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten representative login input/focus cycles, heap self-size rose only 59,176 bytes (6,693,096 to 6,752,272; 0.9%), node count by 142, while closure count stayed exactly 8,393.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary and in-page node/heap metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: The loaded page heap summary was about 6.7MB with stable DOM element count of 92, proportionate for the login page and its CAPTCHA/analytics dependencies.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared heap type/constructor summaries and DOM count before/after
checkOutcomes.evidence: Across the repeated interaction, native node population remained effectively flat (18,967 to 18,968), closures stayed 8,393, DOM elements stayed 92, and no Detached* constructor appeared in either top-constructor summary.

principleOutcomes.reason: Agent-facing capabilities are contextual and the site declares no agentic intent. There is no user task on these public surfaces that calls for on-device inference.

paths.description: Landing/login template: primary sign-in, consent, preference, performance, privacy, security, responsiveness, and no-JS evidence.
Signup promotion template: acquisition message and route into account creation.
Registration step 1: representative primary form, consent, CAPTCHA, keyboard path, and invalid submission.
Password-recovery index: account recovery options and navigation.
Public reviews listing: distinct content/list template, long-scroll navigation, form, dates, and metadata.
Help index: distinct support/navigation template including safety and account-deletion links.
Synthetic missing route that returned a real HTTP 404, used to judge recovery behavior.
Authenticated profiles, matching/search, messaging, payments, and account management were not covered because no test credentials were provided and login is CAPTCHA-protected.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the light capture; body and form surfaces remain fixed pale cream/white and the DOM CSS contains no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, control, and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: Text and controls do not adapt to increased contrast and several fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more capture does not adapt the palette, and axe measured five failures including 1.98:1 for the h1 and 2.49:1 for the cookie button.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system/forced-color-friendly colors, avoid fixed low-contrast orange/green pairs, and test all states at 4.5:1 for normal text.

findings.summary: Primary route changes are abrupt and provide no spatial continuity.
findings.evidence: Navigation among home, registration, recovery, reviews, and help performs abrupt full-document swaps; DOM/CSS inspection found no ::view-transition rules or view-transition-name usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and restrained directional transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long content offers no scroll-state orientation or persistent navigation.
findings.evidence: The long reviews listing has no sticky context, progress, or scroll-state response; its only menu is at the top while pagination appears after the list.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a compact sticky header/back control and a subtle scrollability/progress affordance, progressively enhanced with scroll-state queries.

findings.summary: The on-load cookie banner obscures content and cannot be declined or dismissed.
findings.evidence: A fixed cookie banner occupies roughly the bottom 148px of the 800px mobile viewport on load and presents only a prominent Accept action, obscuring app-store/footer content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface with equally available accept, reject, and settings actions and remember the choice.

findings.summary: Consent uses an ad-hoc pseudo-button and non-semantic overlay.
findings.evidence: The cookie control is a custom <span role="button" tabindex="0"> inside fixed divs, with no dialog/popover semantics and no light-dismiss or reject action.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real button and an appropriate dialog/popover pattern with labelled purpose, focus behavior, and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Components rely on legacy fixed sizing rather than adapting to their available container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no container queries or logical sizing; at 1365px the login form remains a 244px strip while background panels stretch edge-to-edge, showing no component-level adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce a centered intrinsic-width content container and use container queries/logical sizing for reusable forms and listings.

findings.summary: Core login and registration controls are removed from keyboard navigation and several targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: Every login control, recovery link, and registration field has tabindex=-1, removing the core flows from sequential keyboard navigation; many links are only 14–17px tall and the checkbox is 13x13px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove tabindex=-1 from native interactive elements, preserve visible :focus-visible styles, and provide at least 24x24 CSS px targets with 44px preferred for primary touch actions.

findings.summary: The primary authentication and registration journeys exclude keyboard users.
findings.evidence: The login and two-step registration journeys cannot be completed with sequential keyboard input because all controls are tabindex=-1; Turnstile also gates both flows and the invalid registration attempt produced no actionable state.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore native tab order, label all fields, make CAPTCHA provide an accessible alternative, and verify both steps end-to-end by keyboard and assistive technology.

findings.summary: Failure states do not provide clear, actionable recovery.
findings.evidence: After accepting consent and attempting an empty registration submission, the page remained unchanged with no :invalid fields, role=alert, aria-invalid, or error text; the 404 tells users to go back but provides no actionable link.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, move focus to a concise error summary, associate field errors, and add real recovery links on error pages.

findings.summary: Mobile paint performance is slow despite a visually simple page.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 4.3s and FCP 3.7s, outside the good range, although the local desktop trace was faster at 1.35s and CLS remained low.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the initial HTML/CSS and logo, defer non-critical scripts/analytics/CAPTCHA, and retest LCP under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and third-party dependency chains delay a very small page.
findings.evidence: Two 300KB+ parser-inserted legacy scripts in <head> have neither async nor defer; HAR recorded 31 requests, seven redirects, and 484KB transferred, with Turnstile alone delaying about 1.39s.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer/module-load the application bundles, load CAPTCHA only when the auth form is engaged, and remove avoidable redirect chains.

findings.summary: Most of the shipped JavaScript is unused on the landing page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 225KiB of unused JavaScript: 128KB from index.min.js, 54KB from Yandex Metrika, and 48KB from vendor-index.min.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a landing/auth-specific bundle, conditionally import feature code, and delay analytics until consent and idle time.

findings.summary: Core form fields and some links lack accessible names and structure.
findings.evidence: axe reported critical label failures for both login fields, an unnamed tracking link, and missing landmarks; registration fields likewise use nearby text rather than associated <label> elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate explicit labels with every input/select, remove or name the tracking link, and organize content with header/main/nav/footer landmarks.

findings.summary: Important text and controls fail WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe found five serious contrast failures, including the 1.98:1 heading, 1.79:1 online count, 3.94:1 sign-in button, 3.26:1 policy link, and 2.49:1 consent button.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace pale orange/green foregrounds and coral button colors with tested tokens meeting 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text/UI.

findings.summary: Landmark structure is weak and the primary flows are absent from keyboard focus order.
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark and content outside landmarks; more critically, login and registration inputs/buttons are all tabindex=-1 despite showing an outline only when focused programmatically.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic landmarks/headings and native document-order focus; never remove required controls from sequential focus.

findings.summary: Key headings and consent copy are cramped and undersized.
findings.evidence: The primary h1 is rendered at 13px and the consent text at 12px/14px; screenshots show dense low-contrast copy and edge-to-edge rows that reduce reading comfort.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a readable type scale, 1.4–1.6 line-height for body copy, bounded line lengths, and clearer spacing/hierarchy.

findings.summary: Most templates omit mobile scaling metadata and expose undersized/keyboard-inaccessible targets.
findings.evidence: Home, signup, registration, recovery, and help omit the viewport meta; the target probe found 13x13 and 14–17px-high controls, while core CAPTCHA canvas interaction has no equivalent exposed in page markup.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 without disabling zoom, enlarge targets, and ensure Turnstile has an accessible non-canvas fallback.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery hints.
findings.evidence: The doctype and charset are valid, but 5 of 6 images omit width/height, four below-fold images are not lazy, and five use legacy PNG/GIF without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio, lazy-load below-fold badges, and provide appropriately sized modern-format sources where beneficial.

findings.summary: The page cannot use BFCache and generates browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports five BFCache blockers (notably Cache-Control: no-store and WebSocket use) plus DevTools cookie issues; deprecated APIs, paste prevention, and on-load permission prompts did pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Limit no-store to truly sensitive responses, close/restore live connections around pagehide/pageshow, and correct cookie attributes.

findings.summary: Most public templates lack meaningful meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: Home has a descriptive title/description, but signup, registration, recovery, and help have no meta description and reviews uses a blank description.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each public template a concise, unique description aligned with its visible purpose.

findings.summary: Crawlable pages inconsistently declare mobile behavior and descriptive link text.
findings.evidence: Links and robots.txt are crawlable, but four of five representative legacy templates omit meta viewport; several app-store links rely solely on images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add consistent viewport metadata and ensure image links retain descriptive accessible/crawler-visible text.

findings.summary: The sitemap exposes stale HTTP-era indexing signals.
findings.evidence: Responses and canonicals are valid, but the sitemap index lists only http:// URLs and every lastmod is 2021-09-12 despite currently changing profile/review content.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish HTTPS sitemap locations, refresh lastmod only when content changes, and keep sitemap/canonical hosts intentionally aligned.

findings.summary: Public entity and review pages lack structured and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD or Open Graph tags were present on the organization landing page or public review listing, despite these representing a service/organization and user reviews.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite metadata and appropriate review/list metadata, plus Open Graph preview fields matching visible content.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are all absent; sid and test cookies lack Secure and SameSite protection.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy/Permissions-Policy, and Secure HttpOnly SameSite auth cookies.

findings.summary: Tracking begins before meaningful consent and dominates the request surface.
findings.evidence: While the only consent UI is still visible, Yandex Metrika and LiveInternet load; HAR recorded 25 of 31 requests and 468KB of 484KB from other origins, including repeated Yandex cookie-sync chains.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize non-essential analytics before an affirmative choice; offer reject/settings, minimize events, and remove cookie-sync/legacy counters where possible.

findings.summary: Authentication remains password-only with no phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse confirms no geolocation/notification prompt on load, but both public authentication and registration expose password-only flows; no WebAuthn/passkey capability is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration/sign-in and recovery alongside existing methods, requested only from explicit user actions.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Neither CSP frame-ancestors nor X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Trusted Types enforcement, or origin-isolation headers were observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors and Trusted Types where feasible, nosniff, restrictive referrer/permissions policies, and evaluate COOP/COEP needs.

findings.summary: The app-like service is not meaningfully installable and has no offline fallback.
findings.evidence: This app-like dating service exposes a manifest, but it contains only name "App" and one 192px icon, with no start_url/display/short_name; no service-worker registrations exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a complete web app manifest and a narrowly scoped service worker with an offline shell/recovery page for public/auth surfaces.

findings.summary: Network/error recovery surfaces are informational but not actionable.
findings.evidence: The real 404 returns status 404 and explains the problem, but offers only plain-text instructions to go back, no Home/Retry link; no offline fallback is registered.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Home, Back, and Retry actions to 404/network states and provide an offline fallback for key public routes.

findings.summary: Most templates do not expose a valid document language and use physical CSS.
findings.evidence: Home, recovery, reviews, and registration use xml:lang or no language instead of a valid HTML lang attribute; axe flags html-has-lang, and the CSS capability probe found no logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Set <html lang="ru" dir="ltr"> consistently and migrate layout declarations to logical properties so translation/writing-mode changes remain safe.

findings.summary: Human-readable review times omit machine-readable locale-neutral values.
findings.evidence: The reviews template renders Russian relative dates such as “вчера в 21:54” in <time> elements without datetime values, leaving no machine-readable instant and no evidence of locale-aware formatting.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit ISO datetime attributes and format relative dates with Intl.RelativeTimeFormat from canonical timestamps.

findings.summary: Consent is one-sided and tracking begins before the user can choose.
findings.evidence: The consent banner offers only Accept while analytics and cookie syncing already run; there is no Reject or Settings control, making the apparent choice non-reversible and non-neutral.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential tracking by default and present equal accept/reject/settings choices without manipulative emphasis.

findings.summary: Invalid registration fails silently instead of explaining what to correct.
findings.evidence: After accepting terms and attempting an empty registration submission, no visible error, :invalid field, aria-invalid state, role=alert, or focused recovery target appeared; the CAPTCHA remained in “Verifying...” state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints and post-interaction validation, associate concise errors with fields, announce a summary, and move focus predictably.

findings.summary: Authentication fields do not support standard autofill or keyboard input order.
findings.evidence: Login and registration text/password/date fields have empty autocomplete values and tabindex=-1; fields rely on nearby text rather than explicit labels, preventing autofill and keyboard assistance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens (username, current-password, new-password, name, bday fields), explicit labels, inputmode, and native focus order.

findings.summary: Account onboarding bundles consent and excludes safer, accessible authentication choices.
findings.evidence: The audited account-creation/sign-in flows are password-only, keyboard-inaccessible, gated by a canvas CAPTCHA, and combine terms, cookies, and personal-data consent into one required checkbox.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate required contractual acceptance from optional cookie choices, restore accessible controls/CAPTCHA alternatives, and add passkey onboarding and reauthentication.

findings.summary: Image delivery omits modern sizing and loading optimizations.
findings.evidence: Five images use legacy PNG/GIF, five omit intrinsic dimensions, four below-fold images are not lazy, and no image uses srcset; transferred image weight is modest at 36KB but delivery is not optimized.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, lazy loading below fold, and appropriately sized WebP/AVIF or SVG sources where they reduce bytes.

findings.summary: Unused code and pre-consent analytics consume resources without immediate user value.
findings.evidence: A simple server-rendered login page transfers 428KB of script and Lighthouse estimates 225KiB unused; analytics triggers multiple cookie-sync redirects before consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship a minimal route bundle, conditionally load CAPTCHA/features, and defer/batch consented analytics.

findings.summary: Third-party work dominates the page’s network budget.
findings.evidence: 25 of 31 requests and 468KB of 484KB transferred came from other origins; Yandex, Cloudflare, and LiveInternet account for substantial script/network activity on a minimal login view.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget, remove redundant counters, gate analytics on consent, and lazy-load CAPTCHA only when needed.
